text:
jamie: Morning handoff (07:00 UTC). Primary -> @sree, Secondary -> @linh. Quick TL;DR: two pages in the last 12h, both mitigated but a few follow-ups remain. See details below. :coffee:

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident alert: KV-cache spike (INC-4271) — 03/13 23:15 UTC -> 03/14 01:05 UTC. Pages sent to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished for runtime rollback to v1.9.2 at 00:50 UTC (rolled from v1.9.4) — trigger: emergency rollback for INC-4271.

sree: Full summary from runtime side — KV-cache TTL churn caused a cascade of cache misses on sandboxes and small prod customers. Symptoms: elevated 5xxs (~8% peak) and token CPU spikes on a subset of GPU hosts. Impact window ~23:10-00:45 UTC.

linh: What caused the TTL churn? Any config flips?

sree: We traced it to an interaction between the new prefix-caching optimization and a recently landed mempool GC change. Under a particular access pattern the prefix cache entries were evicted aggressively which produced a storm of inference cold-starts. Root cause: kernel selection path didn't propagate the new cache hints.

maria: Customers impacted: ~12 sandbox orgs + 3 small prod clients on dedicated pool dp-7. No enterprise customers hit (as far as we can tell). Replicated request rates and logs attached in incident channel.

jamie: Mitigation timeline (concise):
- 23:25 UTC: throttled sandbox traffic to reduce cache churn (quick stopgap).
- 23:40 UTC: scaled dp-7 up by +20% capacity to absorb cold starts.
- 00:10 UTC: disabled prefix-caching optimization via runtime flag (hotfix toggle).
- 00:50 UTC: rolled runtime back to v1.9.2 to be safe.
- 01:05 UTC: 5xx rates returned to baseline. :white_check_mark:

oliver: Embeddings p99 noise (INC-4274) — flagged at 02:20 UTC. Symptoms: p99 latency bumped to ~2.3s on the embed shard in us-west for ~45 minutes. Root cause: hot shard from imbalanced placement after autoscale shuffle. Mitigation: forced rebalance, increased replica count, and tuned admission control. Now stable.

sree: Current status (as of last check 07:00 UTC):
- INC-4271 KV-cache: resolved, runtime v1.9.2 in prod. Monitoring: KV miss rate and 5xx near baseline but watching for regression.
- INC-4274 Embedding p99: resolved, replica count increased and autoscaler rule adjusted.
- Open alerts: one noisy health probe alert on dp-2 (low priority) — currently suppressed for 2h while infra runs cleanup.

jamie: Customer impact assessment: small subset of customers experienced latency and occasional 5xx. No data loss reported. Support has notified impacted orgs with default mitigation steps and offer to escalate if they see residual errors.

linh: Known follow-ups (action items):
- Runtime: add a guard in kernel-selection to respect prefix-cache hints (owner: @sree, due EOD next business day).
- Infra: add a canary test that runs prefix/cold-start workload before runtime rollout (owner: @oliver, PR under review).
- Ops: update the runbook section "KV cache cascade" with the rollback checklist and throttling commands (owner: @jamie, due tomorrow).
- Monitoring: add a composite alert for simultaneous KV miss + token CPU spike (owner: observability team, ticket created).

sree: Quick runbook pointers (links):
- Runtime rollback: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-rollback (use flag `--force-rollback` and verify KV miss metrics)
- Throttle sandboxes: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/traffic-shaping (#sandbox-profile)
- Embedding shard rebalance: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-rebalance

jamie: Handoff notes for next 12h shift:
- Primary: @sree (watch KV miss rate and 5xx).
- Secondary: @linh (cover embedding shard health and autoscaler anomalies).
- Paging escalation: if KV miss rate > 2x baseline for >5m, page eng-runtime and eng-sre. Use escalation list in runbook.
- On-call rotations: pager contacts are on the runbook, but immediate phone escalation for customer-impacting incidents: @oliver (infra lead) -> @maria (support lead).

linh: Coverage gap note: APAC night (00:00-06:00 UTC) currently has only one oncall in rotation; we should consider a follow-the-sun backup or schedule overlap for releases. Filing a separate scheduling RFC.

maria: Support follow-ups: ticket templates ready for the 12 impacted orgs. Will reopen tickets if they report errors. Verified that none of our enterprise customers reported faults.

jamie: Anything else urgent before I sign off?

sree: I'll keep an eye on the composite alert and the canary run. No active mitigation required right now.

oliver: I'll push the autoscaler tweak to staging and add a short-lived metric to detect placement imbalance.

jamie: Thanks all. Handoff complete. Next check-in at 13:00 UTC unless pages come in. :v:

oncall-bot: Scheduled check-in reminder set for 13:00 UTC.

-- end of thread --
